name: Miles Solar Playbook
label: Solar
summary: Sell the monthly bill, not the panels: in 2026 homeowners who buy get no federal credit, so lead with leases/PPAs or financed savings, and qualify hard on roof, shade and utility rules. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: Intro
lines: Sell the monthly bill, not the panels: in 2026 homeowners who buy get no federal credit, so lead with leases/PPAs or financed savings, and qualify hard on roof, shade and utility rules. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: 1. At a glance
lines: Planned, long cycle (weeks to months), high ticket
Free savings analysis using the homeowner's actual utility bill

The 30% homeowner credit (25D) ended for systems after Dec 31, 2025. Third-party-owned systems (leases, PPAs, prepaid leases) can still carry a business credit (48E), with a placed-in-service deadline at the end of 2027 for projects not safe-harbored
Lease / PPA with low or $0 down; batteries for outage-prone areas; state incentives and net metering where they exist
Roof age and condition, orientation and shade, homeownership, credit for financing, utility rate

sections.title: 2. Seasonality by region
lines: Sales run year-round; bills and installs drive the peaks.
Sell in fall/winter for spring installs

Deadline marketing: projects relying on the business credit must be placed in service by Dec 31, 2027 unless safe-harbored, so expect a "speed over spec" rush through 2027. Only use deadline copy that matches the installer's financing partners.

sections.title: 3. Location signals (add to ZIP score)
lines: Utility rates and net metering / export rules for the ZIP's utility (the biggest driver of savings).
State incentives and property/sales tax exemptions.
Owner-occupied single-family share; roof age (re-roof before solar if the roof is 15+ years old).
Sun exposure and tree cover; outage frequency (battery demand).
Income and credit profile for financing vs lease.

sections.title: 4. Demographics and audiences
lines: Savings buyer: homeowner 35–65 with high electric bills; wants a clear monthly number.
Resilience buyer: outage-prone areas; wants battery backup.
Values buyer: environmentally motivated, higher income; wants ownership and quality equipment.
Audiences: homeowners in high-rate utility territories, EV owners, past roofing/electrical customers (cross-sell), retargeting to calculator users.

Load with the Audience framework in the Master Template. Emergency segments get no income or homeowner filter and start at 25+; planned segments use the filters below. Ages are starting points: Miles tightens them from closed-won CRM data after 30 booked jobs.
high utility rates; net metering available; roof age under 15 yrs or bundle re-roof; low tree cover
Advantage+ on; suggestion 35-65; qualifying lead form (owner, utility, bill, roof age)
Search: solar panels [city], solar lease; observe Homeowners; exclude Renters
Search: solar battery, home battery backup
Exclude in every segment: customers from the last 12 months (except retention campaigns), open leads and estimates, employees, out-of-area ZIPs.

sections.title: 5. Offer stack
lines: Free bill-based savings analysis + satellite roof design
$[0] down, fixed rate [¢]/kWh or $[X]/mo, escalator disclosed
Financed system from $[X]/mo; state incentives listed
Battery storage, EV charger, critter guard, roof replacement bundle
Annual production check; panel cleaning; referral credit after a referred system is installed

sections.title: 6. Channels and campaign build
lines: Search: "solar panels [city]", "solar lease", "solar battery"; negatives: jobs, DIY kits, portable panels, "free solar" scam terms.
Meta: bill-savings creative, customer bill-before/after (with consent), battery backup; lead form with utility and homeownership questions.
Qualify before booking: homeowner, utility, monthly bill, roof age, shade. Book in-home or virtual design consults.
Long nurture: 30–90 day email/SMS sequence with savings examples and FAQs.

sections.title: 7. Triggers Miles watches
lines: Rate-hike savings campaign in that utility's ZIPs
Pause and rewrite offers before any ad runs again

sections.title: 8. After the job and retention
lines: Install day photos; production monitoring set up; 30-day savings check.
Thank-you credit toward a service visit; honest review ask to everyone.
Referral program paid after the referred system is installed; neighbor postcards around installs.

sections.title: 9. Compliance and watch-outs
lines: Never claim a federal tax credit for homeowner-purchased systems in 2026; never say "free solar" or imply a government program.
Lease/PPA ads must state it's a lease or PPA, the term, and any escalator; savings claims need assumptions shown.
Many states regulate door-to-door and solar sales disclosures; follow state rules and the financing partner's ad guidelines.
Recheck incentive copy every quarter; this area changed fast in 2025–2026.

sections.title: 10. Deploy checklist
lines: ☐ Confirm business model (lease/PPA partners, purchase financing, batteries) and licensed areas
☐ Score ZIPs on utility rate, net metering, homeownership, roof age, outages
☐ Load offers with real lease/PPA terms; legal check on every claim
☐ Build Search + Meta with qualifying lead form; savings-analysis landing page
☐ Turn on long nurture, consult reminders, post-install and referral automations
Sources: 25D ended; 48E for leases/PPAs (Solar.com) · TPO deadlines (EnergySage) · 2027 install deadline and market shift (pv magazine)
